narrativeReportMd:
# Binary R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No direct local structural breaking change was found for `Binary`: the local elements, cardinalities, datatypes, `Reference(Resource)` target, required MIME binding strength, modifier flags, and summary flags are stable. The one material local issue is a semantic/conversion risk: R4 Binary text explicitly mentioned `Media` as image/security-context guidance, while R6 removes those `Media` references and the R6 core package no longer contains `StructureDefinition/Media`.

## Scope
The analysis is scoped to the Binary resource StructureDefinition and directly related MIME ValueSet metadata. Inherited `Resource` and `Element` changes are recorded as out of scope and are not counted as Binary findings.

## Main migration themes
Most R4 Binary instances with `contentType`, optional `securityContext`, and optional `data` should validate structurally the same way in R6. Systems that used `Binary.securityContext.reference` values such as `Media/123`, or that followed the R4 recommendation that Media was preferred for images, need a cross-version policy because R6 Binary no longer presents Media as the related resource example and the R6 package has no Media resource definition.

## Highest-impact findings
The only finding is `Binary:SEMANTIC_OR_CONFORMANCE_TEXT:Binary.securityContext:media-guidance`, a potential R4-to-R6 migration/runtime issue rather than a guaranteed Binary-shape validation failure.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is warranted for installations that stored image binaries and used R4 Media resources as security proxies, because the supplied inputs do not include the official Media migration rationale or a normative conversion map.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The local Binary element model stayed backward compatible. A less disruptive migration experience could have been provided by preserving explicit cross-version guidance for legacy Media references, but retaining Media as an R6 example would be misleading if Media is no longer a valid R6 resource.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Binary has no direct local element-shape break from R4 to R6. The main migration concern is legacy use of `Media` with Binary image/security-context workflows; the top uncertainty is the absence of official Media/Binary migration notes in the inspected inputs.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly a no-op for the Binary resource shape: keep `contentType`, `data`, and `securityContext` as before. The exception is reference and workflow migration around R4 `Media`: if a Binary used `Media/…` as a security context or if image-handling logic expected a Media companion resource, R6 systems need an explicit replacement target such as `DocumentReference`, `Observation`, another clinically appropriate resource, or a local extension/profile policy.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that local Binary element presence, cardinality, types, reference target profile, flags, and required MIME binding strength are unchanged because these are directly visible in both StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for the Media-related impact because the local Binary text changed and the R6 package lacks `StructureDefinition-Media.json`, but the supplied inputs do not include official migration rationale, rendered narrative, or conversion maps.

findings.title: Binary no longer gives Media-oriented guidance for images or security context

oldState.summary: R4 Binary text explicitly connected Binary image handling and securityContext examples to Media.

semanticText.definition: This element identifies another resource that can be used as a proxy of the security sensitivity to use when deciding and enforcing access control rules for the Binary resource. Given that the Binary resource contains very few elements that can be used to determine the sensitivity of the data and relationships to individuals, the referenced resource stands in as a proxy equivalent for this purpose. This referenced resource may be related to the Binary (e.g. Media, DocumentReference), or may be some non-related Resource purely as a security proxy. E.g. to identify that the binary resource relates to a patient, and access should only be granted to applications that have access to the patient.
semanticText.comment: At the root, R4 also said that Media was preferred for handling images when possible.

oldState.narrativeMd: `Binary.securityContext` was still a generic `Reference(Resource)`, but R4 explicitly named `Media` alongside `DocumentReference` as a related resource that could stand in as the security proxy. The root Binary comment also guided image use toward the Media resource.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same Binary.securityContext shape but removes the Media example and the root Media-preference image note.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Binary.securityContext` has the same element id/path, cardinality, type, target profile, and flags in both versions. The delta is only in local semantic text and related-resource guidance.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a guaranteed Binary element validation break: `Binary.securityContext` remains `0..1 Reference(Resource)`. The potential break appears when an R4 Binary uses `securityContext.reference` such as `Media/123`, or application code assumes a Media companion resource for image binaries. An R6 validator or runtime that checks reference resource types against the R6 package may not recognize `Media`, and generated R6 models/resource-type enums will not have a Media class to resolve or authorize against.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `Binary.securityContext` is explicitly about access control. A failed or lossy migration of the proxy reference can lead to over-restricting legitimate access or, worse, applying the wrong access-control context to binary content.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Binary guidance with the R6 resource set by no longer presenting Media as the preferred or example related resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking Binary base-design alternative was identified; the plausible aids are legacy Media migration guidance or conversion rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: if `Media` is no longer part of the R6 core resource set, Binary should not continue presenting it as a preferred image resource or ordinary `securityContext` example. The local Binary shape already preserves the R4 element, cardinality, and `Reference(Resource)` target, so the remaining disruption comes from legacy `Media/...` references and workflows rather than from a narrower Binary element design. Without official Media migration rationale this is not fully proven, but the level of Binary-local breakage appears probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The previously described less-disruptive path--adding a legacy note, ConceptMap, or conversion recipe for R4 `Media` security contexts--would be useful migration support, but calibration treats that as mitigation rather than a backward-compatible base-design alternative. A true base-design alternative such as leaving `Media` in the R6 Binary examples would preserve familiar prose for some R4 implementers, but would fail the apparent R6 goal by implying that `Media` remains an ordinary R6 resource target. No less-breaking Binary base design that both preserves legacy `Media` semantics and accurately reflects the R6 resource set was identified.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Migration notes or ConceptMaps would reduce ambiguity but are mitigations, not a backward-compatible base R6 Binary design; retaining Media as ordinary R6 guidance would conflict with the R6 resource set.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are illustrative. The R4 fragment relies on an external `Media/123` resource that would need to exist and carry the intended security context. The R6 migration example uses `DocumentReference/123` only as a common candidate replacement; the correct target must be chosen from the actual clinical/workflow context.

findings.narrativeMd: `Binary.securityContext` did not structurally narrow its reference target, but the Binary-specific guidance changed in a way that matters for real migrations. R4 told readers that a related resource could be `Media` and that Media was preferred for images when the content was not already constrained by binary-only workflows. R6 removes both Media-oriented statements, and the R6 core package inspected here does not contain a Media resource. Existing R4 systems that used Media as the authorization proxy for a Binary cannot assume that the same literal reference or generated model relationship remains valid in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A plain R6 Binary shape validator may still accept the `securityContext` element because its type remains `Reference(Resource)`. The break appears in stricter validation or runtime resolution: `Media/123` names a resource type absent from the R6 package, so a validator, resolver, generated enum, or authorization service may reject it or fail to resolve the proxy. This is therefore a potential old-valid/new-invalid or old-working/new-failing pattern, not a universal instance break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 Binary records whose `securityContext.reference` starts with `Media/` and any image workflows that paired Binary with Media. Decide the R6 authorization proxy resource case by case: `DocumentReference` may fit document-like binaries, while other image/device/observation workflows may need another R6 resource, a profile rule, or an extension. Test both validation and authorization behavior, not just JSON parsing, because the risk is in reference resolution and access-control semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The local Binary structure remained backward-compatible; the disruptive part is the removal of a formerly recommended/example related resource. If Media is gone from R6, retaining it as a normal example would be incorrect. A backward-compatible migration aid could still have preserved a legacy note, ConceptMap, or conversion recipe so R4 `Media` security contexts could be transformed without implementers reverse-engineering the intended replacement.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 narrative or ballot notes whether Media was intentionally removed, renamed, or folded into another workflow-specific resource. If a separate Media migration report exists, this Binary finding should link to it rather than duplicating the Media resource identity analysis.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 and R6 keep `Binary.securityContext` as `0..1 Reference(Resource)` with the same access-control role, so this is not a Binary-local cardinality, type, or binding break. The meaningful migration issue is narrower: an R4 Binary that used `securityContext.reference` to point at a `Media` resource may not resolve cleanly in R6 because the R6 package no longer defines `Media`, and generated R6 clients or validators may not have a Media resource type. That can affect authorization proxy logic, but it is largely a consequence of removing the low-maturity Media resource rather than a new restriction on Binary itself.
keyEvidence: R4 `Binary.securityContext` definition says the related proxy resource may be `Media` or `DocumentReference`; R6 keeps `DocumentReference` but removes `Media` from the example.
R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions both define `Binary.securityContext` as `0..1 Reference(Resource)` with `isSummary: true` and `isModifier: false`.
R4 package contains `StructureDefinition-Media.json`; R6 package index and file glob show no `StructureDefinition-Media.json`.
R4 maturity data: Binary is normative/FMM 5, while Media is trial-use/FMM 1.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Binary's normative/FMM 5 status raises the burden for direct breaks on this access-control element, but the specific compatibility hazard depends on preserving the separate R4 Media resource, which was only trial-use/FMM 1; that softens the case for requiring R6 to keep Media solely for Binary securityContext compatibility.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen, with possible old-valid/new-invalid behavior in validators that reject `Media/...` references because R6 has no Media resource type. The Binary element shape itself did not become narrower.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A Binary-local less-breaking design is limited: the target is already the broad `Reference(Resource)`, and keeping `Media` in Binary prose while Media is absent would be misleading and would not preserve runtime resolvability. A true compatibility design would require retaining a legacy Media resource or alias in base R6, which is a broader top-level design choice with ongoing API, validation, and code-generation cost for an FMM 1 resource. Adding clearer migration guidance would help implementers but would not be a less-breaking base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact judgment: there is a real migration risk for Binary securityContext values that point to Media, especially because securityContext drives access control. I would frame it as a proportionate runtime/codegen migration issue rather than a strong Binary-local hard break; I agree that there is no obvious low-cost less-breaking Binary design.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Both versions use canonical `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Binary`, id/name/type `Binary`, kind `resource`, abstract `false`, base `Resource`, derivation `specialization`, and status `active`.
The locally defined Binary element set is unchanged: root `Binary`, `Binary.contentType`, `Binary.securityContext`, and `Binary.data`.
`Binary.contentType` remains `1..1`; `Binary.securityContext` and `Binary.data` remain `0..1`; the root remains `0..*` in the StructureDefinition.

`Binary.securityContext.type.targetProfile` remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Resource`. Changes to which concrete resources exist in R6 are outside the local Binary target-profile declaration.

`Binary.contentType` remains a required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/mimetypes`; the version suffix changes from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`. Both inspected ValueSets compose all codes from `urn:ietf:bcp:13`, but no live terminology expansion comparison was performed.
No Binary-specific invariant was added, removed, or strengthened. The copied `ele-1` constraint is sourced from `Element` and is treated as inherited/base-artifact scope.
No local Binary element has a fixed value, pattern, or default value in either version.
No local Binary element introduced or removed maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue limits.
The root and local elements remain non-modifier elements. Inherited `Resource.implicitRules` remains out of scope.
`Binary.contentType` and `Binary.securityContext` remain summary elements; `Binary.data` and the root remain non-summary.
No slicing is defined on local Binary elements in either StructureDefinition.

The local StructureDefinition shape does not add, remove, rename, or retype any serialized Binary property. R6 contains XML schema artifacts for Binary, but no comparable R4 package XML schema file was found in the inspected package path, so this check relies on the StructureDefinitions.

R6 adds no local Binary element or datatype that R4 Binary lacks. R6-to-R4 representability risks for references to R6-only resource types are generic `Reference(Resource)` issues and are not Binary-local.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Binary.contentType MIME ValueSet version changes to the R6 ballot version
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains `required` and the value set canonical remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/mimetypes`. The inspected R4 and R6 ValueSets both include all codes from `urn:ietf:bcp:13`, so no local required-binding narrowing was found.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology servers and generated validators should load the R6 package version of the ValueSet. Because BCP-13 is external and effectively open-ended, production validation should be tested with the terminology server actually used by the implementation.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly serializes mustSupport=false on local Binary elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omits `mustSupport` on the local Binary elements while R6 serializes `mustSupport: false`. In FHIR StructureDefinitions, absence and explicit false have the same conformance meaning for these base elements.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or diff tools should normalize missing boolean flags to false before reporting conformance changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher/contact/jurisdiction and mapping metadata were refreshed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 updates package metadata, adds jurisdiction, changes publisher/contact text, and adds/changes mapping metadata such as a W5 mapping. These are artifact metadata/modeling aids, not instance content constraints.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that compares mappings or publisher metadata may see differences, but instance validation and generated Binary properties are not affected.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 Binary guidance explicitly referred to Media, and R4 contained a Media resource. R6 Binary removes that guidance and the R6 package lacks Media, so the Media resource identity/removal/mapping report should own the definitive migration path.
Binary snapshots include inherited `Resource` elements whose text and terminology may differ across releases. Those inherited changes were excluded here under the base-artifact scope rule.

The copied `ele-1` constraint appears on local Binary elements but is sourced from `Element`; XPath-expression serialization changes and any invariant semantics should be assessed in the Element report.
